name: Reza Saadi
bio: I am a PhD student in Computational Sciences and Engineering at Koç University, advised by Mehmet Cengiz Onbaşlı. My research focuses on post-quantum cryptography and privacy-preserving machine learning, with additional work in secure multiparty computation and theoretical cryptography. During my MSc at Koç University, I worked with Prof. Alptekin Küpçü on security models, proofs, and implementations for distributed single-password authentication.

researchAreas.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography and Quantum Information
researchAreas.summary: I study authenticated key exchange, timing leakage in post-quantum implementations, and mutually unbiased bases in dimension six.

projects.title: AEGIS–VAKE
projects.summary: AEGIS provides structural checks for authenticated key-exchange models. VAKE studies which Lean proofs can be reused when a protocol changes. The Rust and Lean interpreters agreed on all 188 tested executions. A signing-origin proof was reused for two controlled signed Diffie–Hellman revisions under trusted credentials and a symbolic attacker model.

projects.title: Timing Leakage in Post-Quantum Implementations
projects.summary: Combines instruction analysis with end-to-end timing experiments to study when known Kyber timing effects are measurable on Intel processors.

projects.title: Computational mutually unbiased bases in ℂ⁶
projects.summary: Searches for four approximately mutually unbiased bases using Riemannian optimization and minimax refinement. Rational certificates give upper bounds on the achieved deviation.

researchAreas.title: Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning and ML Theory
